finding.message: `values` is a lazy sequence and is consumed twice. `values` produces its elements only when consumed, and it is consumed more than once. The second pass throws, sees nothing, or repeats all the work.

presentation.description: `values` produces its elements only when consumed, and it is consumed more than once. The second pass throws, sees nothing, or repeats all the work.

derivedFacts: `values` is a lazy, single-pass or re-evaluating sequence
this function consumes it more than once along one path

presentation.more: `values` produces its elements only when it is consumed, and this function consumes it more than once. Depending on what it is, the second pass throws (a Java stream), sees nothing at all because the first pass used everything up (an iterator or generator), or runs the whole pipeline again (a query or a sequence) — none of which is what the code reads as doing. Collect it into a list once and use the list, or build a fresh sequence for each pass.
